The Tax Administrator's office at 200 Montezuma Street in Newland keeps property records, sets assessments and bills the taxes. It has two divisions: assessment at 828-733-8214 and collections at 828-733-8228. Hours are 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

Assessor mail goes to PO Box 305, Newland, NC 28657, and collection mail goes to PO Box 355 in the same town. An online lookup shows real estate, sales and tax bills, and a separate viewer shows tax maps.

Maps and records exist for valuation. The legal description of a parcel is whatever the recorded deed says, so read the deed rather than trusting a map line.

For tax years 2023 through 2025 the county rate is 0.335 and the fire rate is 0.065, a total of 0.40. Ask the tax office how those figures apply to a bill. Towns that levy their own tax add a municipal rate on top, and each town has a code.

The county and fire rates apply to every parcel, and the town rate applies only where a town levies one. Ask the tax office which codes your parcel carries. Ten fire districts cover the county: Banner Elk, Crossnore, Elk Park, Fall Creek, Green Valley, Linville, Newland, Frank, Beech Mountain and Seven Devils.

Current values were set as of January 1, 2022, and notices went out that March. Counties must reappraise real property at least once in eight years, and the goal is a tax value that matches what a willing buyer and seller would agree on.

The county did the work with its own staff instead of hiring an outside appraisal firm. Its revaluation guide includes a sales ratio table for houses: 344 sales at a 91 percent ratio in 2018, 430 sales at 83 percent in 2019, 699 sales at 71 percent in 2020 and 675 sales at 60 percent in 2021. A ratio of 100 percent would mean tax value equals sale price, so values had drifted well below sale prices before the 2022 reset.

Owning a house for decades does not earn a lower value. State law requires uniform appraisal, so a long-held home is valued like comparable homes that sold recently.

Start with the informal review named on the value notice. It is not an appeal. Use it to correct facts on your record, learn how the number was built and compare similar parcels. If you are still unhappy, ask in writing for a formal hearing.

The appeal board is made up of appointed taxpaying citizens rather than commissioners. It sits between the first Monday of April and the first Monday of May, and requests must arrive by final adjournment, which is 3:00 p.m. on the closing Monday. Send appeal forms several days before adjournment so hearings can be scheduled. Sessions begin at 9:00 a.m. in courthouse Conference Room 106.

  • Pick up the application at the assessor's office or download it from the county site.
  • Bring record cards and sale prices for similar parcels nearby.
  • The board asks whether the value is accurate and fair. Ability to pay is outside its scope.

A further appeal goes to the Property Tax Commission, by notice within 30 days of the board's mailed decision.

Three state programs plus a farm program are offered, and one owner can claim only one of the first three. Pick up forms from the tax department and return them to the assessor by June 1.

  • Age 65 or disability exclusion: shelters the larger of $25,000 or half the appraised value of a permanent home, with income capped at $38,800 for 2026.
  • Circuit breaker deferment: limits the bill to 4 percent of income when income is at or under $38,800 and to 5 percent when it is at or under $58,200 (2026 figures). The excess is deferred and carried as a lien, and you reapply annually.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: removes up to $45,000 of appraised value with no age or income test. An unmarried surviving spouse may also qualify.
  • Present use value: farmers with active income from land can ask the office for the criteria and an application.

Deferred taxes matter in a sale. When a circuit breaker owner transfers the property, the last three years of deferred taxes come due with interest on the transfer date.

Owners list taxable property during January, and the duty is on the taxpayer even if a form never arrives. Items to list include untagged motor vehicles and motor homes, multi-year tagged trailers, improvements to real estate, income-producing personal property, business equipment, single-wide mobile homes, furnished rental property, and airplanes, boats and motors. Relief applications are taken at listing time too.

State law lets the commissioners extend the period by up to 30 days in a non-revaluation year. An individual with good cause can file a written request for more time before the regular period ends, though no extension runs past April 15.

sections.h2: Questions to ask the tax office before you list
sections.html: A ten-minute call can head off surprises. Ask which town code and fire district your parcel carries, so you know the full rate a buyer will see. Ask whether any exclusion, deferment or present use status is attached to the parcel, since a deferment can bring back three years of tax at transfer. Ask when the next revaluation is expected, because a buyer will want to know. And ask whether the mailing address on file is current, especially if the house is a seasonal one that sits empty part of the year.

Bills are due September 1 and carry no interest until January 6, when 2 percent applies. After February 1, three-quarters of a percent accrues each month. The lien attaches on the listing date, so an unpaid bill stays with the parcel through a sale.

Median owner-occupied value is $265,800, and the county has 14,597 housing units against 6,791 households. With so many seasonal homes, bills often go to a second address, so make sure the tax office has a current mailing address.

Before closing, take these steps:

  • Call collections at 828-733-8228 for the exact balance, including any earlier year.
  • Call assessment at 828-733-8214 about any exclusion or deferment on the parcel.
  • Give the figures to the closing attorney so the bill is paid from the proceeds.
  • Give the township or town along with the parcel details so the right rates are applied.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Avery County tax office?
faqs.a: Assessment is 828-733-8214 and collections is 828-733-8228. Visit 200 Montezuma Street in Newland between 8:00 a.m. and 4:30 p.m.

faqs.q: What is the Avery County tax rate?
faqs.a: The county rate is 0.335 and the fire rate is 0.065, a total of 0.40. Towns add their own rate, from 0.28 in Sugar Mountain to 0.65 in Beech Mountain.

faqs.q: When was Avery County's last revaluation?
faqs.a: Values took effect January 1, 2022. State law requires another within eight years, so ask the tax office for the next schedule.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Avery County property value?
faqs.a: Ask the tax office for an informal review first, then file the written hearing application before the appeal board adjourns, at 3:00 p.m. on the first Monday of May.

faqs.q: Can I get a break on Avery County property tax if I am 65 or disabled?
faqs.a: Yes, when income stays within the 2026 limit of $38,800. The exclusion shelters the larger of $25,000 or half the value, and the assessor must receive the form by June 1.
